cards.explanation: The answer is five. Five men of valor from Zorah and Eshtaol head out to spy out the land and explore it. That's a small crew for a big job. Hold on to that number, friends, because these same five come back into the story.

The answer is his voice. The spies recognize the voice of the young Levite. A voice was all it took. I bet it felt like hearing a familiar ringtone in a strange place. They walk over and start asking questions.

The answer is priest. The Levite says, "Micah has done this and that for me…" and that Micah has hired him to be his priest. "…this and that…" covers a lot, and he doesn't spell it out. Now the spies know what he does in that house, friends.

The answer is whether their journey will succeed. They say, "Please inquire of God to determine whether we will have a successful journey." They want to know before they go. I think anybody who has ever checked the weather three times before a trip understands that feeling. The Levite is the one they ask.

The answer is True. The priest tells them, "Go in peace. The LORD is watching over your journey." That's what the Levite says, word for word. The spies leave with that answer in their ears. Then they head off and come to Laish.

The answer is unsuspecting. The five men see people living securely, like the Sidonians, quiet and unsuspecting. There was nothing lacking in the land and no oppressive ruler. That's what the spies carry home in their report, bakers.

The answer is False. Laish was living securely, like the Sidonians, but the text says they were far away from the Sidonians and had no alliance with anyone. Being like someone and being allied with them are two different things, friends. That detail comes up again when the city falls.

The answer is to go up and take the land. The spies say, "Come on, let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and it is very good." Then they push: "Why would you fail to act? Do not hesitate to go there and take possession of the land!" These guys are not asking for a committee meeting. They want action.

The answer is True. The spies tell their brothers, "…God has delivered it into your hand." They also call it "…a place where nothing on earth is lacking." That's their report, and they sound sure of it. All of this is what they say, and the six hundred set out afterward.

The answer is six hundred. Six hundred Danites depart from Zorah and Eshtaol, armed with weapons of war. Compare that to the five who went to spy, friends. That's a big jump, and a lot of armed men heading out together.

The answer is an ephod and idols. An ephod, household gods, a graven image, and a molten idol, all in ONE house! The spies say, "Did you know that one of these houses has…" and then they just keep going down the list. Friends, that's not a house, that's a whole collection! Then they say, "Now think about what you should do." and leave it hanging right there. That's a hint with no hiding in it, and I love it.

The answer is False. The text says the five men who had gone to spy out the land went inside and took the graven image, the ephod, the household idols, and the molten idol. No money changes hands. The priest stands at the gate with the six hundred armed men the whole time.

The answer is tribe. They ask, "Is it better for you to be a priest for the house of one person or a priest for a tribe and family in Israel?" That's the pitch, friends. One household on one side and a whole tribe on the other. They put it right to him as a question.

The answer is True. The text says the priest was glad. He took the ephod, the household idols, and the graven image, and went with the people. That's the same priest who asked, "What are you doing…" a moment before. By the end of the offer, he's moving.

The answer is that Micah's neighbors chase them down. After they're some distance from Micah's house, the men in the houses near Micah's house mobilized and overtook the Danites. So the neighbors mobilize and catch up. Micah isn't alone in this, and the Danites have to turn around and face them.

The answer is that they took his gods and his priest. Micah says, "You took the gods I had made, and my priest, and went away. What else do I have?" Then he turns their own question back on them: "How can you say to me, ‘What is the matter with you?’…" I think this one hurts a little, friends. His answer is short and plain.

The answer is strong. The text says Micah turned to go back home because he saw that they were too strong for him. The Danites had just said, "Do not raise your voice against us, or angry men will attack you…" Then he saw they were too strong for him, and he went home.

The answer is that they rebuild it and live there. The text says the Danites rebuilt the city and lived there. They had burned it down, and then they settled into it. That's how the tribe finally gets a place, friends.
The answer is Dan. The text says they named it Dan, after their forefather Dan, who was born to Israel. The city was formerly named Laish. So the old name goes out and the family name goes up.

The answer is as long as God's house was in Shiloh. The text says, "…it was there the whole time the house of God was in Shiloh." The Danites set up Micah's graven image for themselves, and it stayed in that spot the entire stretch. That's what Judges 18 closes on, bakers.
